newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees barter possible for Russian jets.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees barter possible for Russian jets.

text.p: Any decision by Indonesia on buying jet fighters and other hardware from Russia appears to hinge on financial arrangements, including the possibility of barter, the Jakarta Post said on Thursday.
The paper quoted Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita as saying the government was still trying to solve the issue of payment for any possible purchases.
"Russia does not provide export credit like Western countries, so we are considering the counter-purchase system," Ginanjar said.
"The potential is there, but the deal could also be carried out using funds from other sources," he said.

Air Force Chief-of-Staff Sutria Tubagus inspected Russian aircraft last month at the Paris Air Show after Indonesia expressed interest in buying Russian Sukhoi-30 and MiG-29 fighters as well as radars, guided missiles and helicopters.
The paper said several Indonesian delegations have visited Moscow this year to discuss the purchases after Russia made an offer in February.
It said Research and Techonology Minister Jusuf Habibie, also head of state-owned plane maker Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN), was reported to be planning a visit to Moscow this month.
Negotiations with Russia gathered momentum after Indonesia cancelled its plan to buy nine American F-16s in May in response to U.S. congressional criticism of Indonesia.
